gloss: to make the first move; to take the initiative

definitions.gloss: to make the first move; to take the initiative; to act preemptively
definitions.explanation: To take action before the other party does, gaining a strategic advantage. Originally from shogi/go terminology where 先手 is the player who moves first.

examples.japanese: {先手|せんて}を{打|う}って⟦{交渉|こうしょう}→交渉：02727_koushou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: I took the initiative and started negotiations.

examples.japanese: ⟦{競合|きょうごう}→競合：05082_kyougou⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{先手|せんて}を{打|う}って⟦{新商品|しんしょうひん}→新商品：11504_shinshouhin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発表|はっぴょう}した→発表する：25231_happyousuru⟧。
examples.english: We got ahead of our competitors by announcing the new product first.

examples.japanese: ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{先手|せんて}を{打|う}って⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{講|こう}じる→講じる：27841_koujiru⟧べきだ。
examples.english: We should take preemptive action and implement countermeasures before the problem grows.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From board game terminology. In shogi and go, ⟦{先手|せんて}→先手：10556_sente⟧ refers to the player who moves first, which is considered an advantage. {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ means to secure that first-mover advantage.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ vs. ⟦{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る→後手に回る：18387_gotenimawaru⟧: Opposite expressions. {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ is proactive; ⟦{後手|ごて}に{回|まわ}る→後手に回る：18387_gotenimawaru⟧ is reactive and disadvantageous.
- ⟦{先|さき}を{越|こ}す→先を越す：16921_sakiwokosu⟧: To get ahead of someone — focuses on outpacing rather than strategic positioning.
- {先制|せんせい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: To strike first, to preempt — more aggressive, often used in military or sports contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}って⟦{対応|たいおう}→対応：02510_taiou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to respond proactively)
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}って⟦{動|うご}く→動く：00904_ugoku⟧ (to act preemptively)
